title: Chicken Francaise
blurb: The lemon-butter sauce reduces in the same pan the chicken was fried in, so the browned bits from frying end up seasoning the sauce instead of going to waste.

ingredients.note: medium, boneless, skinless, cut in half horizontally into cutlets

steps: Preheat oven to 200°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper or foil for easy cleanup. Set a pot of lightly salted water to boil for the pasta.
Cut the chicken breasts in half horizontally into thin, even pieces.
Cover the chicken pieces in plastic wrap and pound with a meat mallet or rolling pin to 1/4-inch thick. Season both sides lightly with salt and pepper.
In a shallow dish, whisk together the flour, salt and pepper. In a second shallow dish, whisk together the eggs and milk.
Dip each chicken piece in the flour until covered, then the egg mixture, then back in the flour, shaking off the excess. Transfer to a plate.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook 2 of the chicken pieces at a time, 1 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and an instant-read thermometer reads 165°F. Transfer to the baking sheet and keep warm in the oven; wipe out the pan and repeat with the remaining oil and chicken.
Add the pasta to the boiling water and cook according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.
Wipe out the skillet and set it over medium heat. Add the butter, and once melted, add the garlic and cook until lightly golden and fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add the chicken stock, wine and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer and cook 8 to 10 minutes, until reduced by a little over half, to about 3/4 cup. Season with salt and pepper to taste and stir in the parsley.
Plate the pasta and chicken and spoon the sauce over the top.
